clue.text: A writer who offered a choice about a coward involved with Juliet

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Thomas Hobson, the Cambridge carrier, offered customers the horse nearest the door or none at all: Hobson's choice

indicators.note: involved suggests letters tangled together, so the letters of a coward with the Juliet letter are rearranged

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone who once gave people an option ends up tangled with a coward and the heroine Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who offered a choice' is Thomas Hobson, the Cambridge carrier whose customers took the horse nearest the door or none: 'Hobson's choice' is a British idiom for no real choice. 'involved with' scrambles; 'about' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Booker-winning British novelist of The Finkler Question is a writer.

clue.text: V. S. Naipaul's work consisting of less than a whole sentence?

definitions.meaning: a 2001 novel by the Trinidad-born Nobel laureate
a prisoner serving only part of a life sentence has served fifty per cent of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks grammatical, but it is a prison term: a life sentence cut in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a Naipaul novel and, read literally, a portion of a life term in jail.

clue.text: English naturalist working with European writer in Australia

definitions.meaning: Gilbert ... wrote The Natural History of Selborne
Patrick ..., London-born Nobel laureate, lived and wrote in Australia

explanation.walkthrough: 'working with' is only a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the Selborne parson-naturalist and to the Nobel-winning author of Voss.

clue.text: Return to the theatre, a long time after a spell away from it?

indicators.note: after places the long-time piece following the spell-away piece

parts.note: a rest is a spell away from work
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An actor comes back to the stage after years away, enjoying a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a play again is to bring it back to the theatre in a new production.

clue.text: Joy's involved with Inspector Len — he's looking for the perfect woman

definitions.text: he's looking for the perfect woman

indicators.note: involved suggests letters entangled, so Joy and Inspector Len are mixed up together

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, leaving the name Joy

explanation.surface: A woman called Joy gets caught up with a police inspector named Len, who is searching for his ideal partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges JOY, INSPECTOR and LEN. The answer is the sculptor in Thomas Hardy's The Well-Beloved, who pursues his ideal woman through three generations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's hero spends his life chasing an idealised beloved embodied in successive women.

clue.text: Applaud one in company at theatre — Juliet's lover

indicators.note: in places the praise-and-one pieces inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: to laud is to praise or applaud
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Theatregoers clap a single performer in the troupe, the one playing Juliet's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at theatre' tells the solver the lover is a stage character: Juliet's lover in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure, not Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: In Measure for Measure the young man condemned for getting Juliet pregnant is her betrothed.

clue.text: A good sort's on the way in a story of an arranged marriage

definitions.text: a story of an arranged marriage

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A decent fellow is on the road, inside a tale of a match made by families.
explanation.walkthrough: 's on' is only a link. Monica Ali's novel follows a Bangladeshi woman sent to London for an arranged marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Monica Ali's 2003 novel tells of Nazneen, married off to an older man in East London.

clue.text: I'm raised, say, in one family Flora Nwapa wrote about

indicators.note: in places the turned-up example abbreviation inside the word one
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A narrator explains she grew up in a particular household in a Nigerian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' is the voice of Nwapa's heroine Efuru, daughter of Nwashike Ogene, so it acts as a link. 'raised' turns the abbreviation upwards, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Nwapa's novel Efuru the heroine's father belongs to this respected family.

clue.text: Prolific British author everyone holds in contempt, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: everyone is all, and to diss is to show contempt for

explanation.surface: A hugely productive writer is said to be despised by all.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Aldiss wrote many science-fiction novels; ALL DISS spoken matches his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Aldiss published scores of novels and stories, mostly science fiction, over sixty years.

clue.text: In Victorian verse she seems dead in criminal cell — a hoax

definitions.text: In Victorian verse she seems dead

indicators.note: in places the hoax pieces inside the rearranged cell
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of cell are rearranged

parts.note: to rib is to tease or play a joke on someone

explanation.surface: A woman in a Victorian poem appears to have died in a prison cell, but it was a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the cell into CLEL. Tennyson's early poem mourns Claribel lying in her grave, hence 'she seems dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's lyric Claribel is a lament for a dead woman of that name.

clue.text: Recent title — it's about life in a new town and Harold Wilson's achievement in 1964

definitions.text: it's about life in a new town and Harold Wilson's achievement in 1964

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
a call is a name or title one is called by

explanation.surface: A newly published book about new-town life marks a Wilson triumph of 1964.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel was published in 1964 by Angus Wilson; the clue teases by swapping in Harold Wilson, who won the general election that year.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus Wilson's 1964 novel follows a retired woman settling into a postwar English new town.

clue.text: Playwright who worked in London recording company, in sound

indicators.note: in sound says the record label's name is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Decca is a British record label

explanation.surface: A dramatist once employed at a London record label.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Dekker was a Jacobean playwright of London life; the label Decca is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Dekker wrote The Shoemaker's Holiday and other city comedies for London theatres.

clue.text: The ego in me is ridiculous in size

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurd and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that their own self-importance is absurdly large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ridiculous' rearranges the letters of THE EGO IN ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers name book formats by how many leaves a sheet is folded into; eighteen leaves gives this small format.

clue.text: Victorian bestseller with a murderer inhabiting a German city

indicators.note: inhabiting means living inside, so the killer goes within the city name

parts.note: Halle is a city in Saxony-Anhalt
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A popular nineteenth-century author keeps company with a killer living in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Hall Caine's melodramatic novels such as The Manxman sold in huge numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hall Caine was among the best-selling novelists of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: A right to depart in a famous ship

parts.note: to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to sail away aboard a celebrated vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's vessel in Greek myth carried the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Sir Charles is one, taken in by a youngster

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the numeral sits within the youngster

parts.note: a grandson is a young member of a family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is fooled by a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it puts I inside GRANDSON. Sir Charles Grandison is Samuel Richardson's novel and its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Richardson's ideal gentleman hero bears this surname, giving the novel its title.

clue.text: Suffer here? An ambassador will

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal style of an ambassador
will is contracted to 'll

explanation.surface: A diplomat agrees to endure hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer here?' defines by example: the place of eternal suffering. HE stands for His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: The place of damnation is where sinners are said to suffer eternally.

clue.text: Indian writer and composer meeting a fool with a kind of intelligence

parts.note: a nit is a fool, so a fool gives A NIT
Thomas Ades is an English composer
AI is artificial intelligence

explanation.surface: A novelist teams up with a musician, an idiot and a computer brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting', 'with' and 'and' are links; the pieces fall in answer order A NIT, ADES, AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita Desai is an Indian novelist, three times shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

clue.text: Dry vegetable matter in a vessel caused trouble

indicators.note: in places the hay-drying verb inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
to ted is to spread mown grass or hay so it dries

explanation.surface: Withered plant material left in a pot became a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an adjective but is a verb: TED, a farming word for turning hay to dry it.
explanation.definitionFit: Misbehaving or malfunctioning is to make trouble, as a child or a machine does.

clue.text: I agree with the German who makes corrections

parts.note: amen expresses agreement, so be it
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone sides with a German proofreader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining AMEN and DER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who revises or alters a text is an editor or reviser of it.

clue.text: Some of his work was valued at 3d (British Sterling)

definitions.text: Some of his work was valued at 3d (British Sterling)

parts.words: Some of his work was valued at 3d (British Sterling)
parts.note: a playwright whose musical play is named after threepence, three old pennies, in its English title

explanation.walkthrough: 3d is three old British pennies; The Threepenny Opera is the famous German play with music by Kurt Weill.
explanation.definitionFit: The German dramatist wrote The Threepenny Opera, whose title prices it at three pence.

clue.text: Answer on the subject of some drama

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
an act is one part of a play

explanation.surface: A reply about a portion of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to answer it.

clue.text: Animal enclosure with many places to sleep, where Ratty lives

parts.note: in Scots a reed is a yard or pen for cattle or other animals
beds are places to sleep

explanation.surface: A farm pen fitted out with plenty of bunks, home to a well-known water rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Ratty is the water vole in The Wind in the Willows, living by the river among the reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A water vole makes its home along riverbanks among thick stands of reeds.

clue.text: Beadle ultimately standing behind a journal of sorts

indicators.note: behind places the final letter after the journal piece

parts.note: a blog is an online journal

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word standing

explanation.surface: A parish officer finally stands behind some kind of diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Blogg is a beadle in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend; a beadle was a minor parish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens names a parish official in Our Mutual Friend with this surname.

clue.text: A short book of the bible is that local oral form of literature

parts.words: A short book of the bible
parts.note: Sam is short for Samuel, a book of the Old Testament
is and that said in a local accent sound like iz and dat

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a brief biblical book counts as regional spoken literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Samizdat was self-published, clandestinely copied writing in the Soviet bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Soviet Union banned texts circulated as secretly typed or copied underground publications.

clue.text: This condition makes Patsy strike

parts.note: drop the S and Y from Patsy and what remains is pat, meaning strike

explanation.surface: A medical complaint leads a woman called Patsy to hit out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: DROP SY. Taking those letters from PATSY leaves PAT, to strike lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for oedema, swelling caused by fluid in the body, is a medical condition.

clue.text: King and queen dwelling in ramshackle hut with swan and vixen

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown, so the letters of hut are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the queen
a pen is a female swan
a vixen is a fierce, quarrelsome woman, and so is a dragon

explanation.surface: Royalty squeeze into a rickety shack with a swan and a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' turns HUT into UTH, and ER joins it to give UTHER. Uther Pendragon is King Arthur's father.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend he was king of Britain and father of Arthur.
